'''Mark Arnold Wainberg''', {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|OQ|FRSC}} (21 April 1945&nbsp;– 11 April 2017) was a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[HIV/AIDS research]]er and [[Activism|HIV/AIDS activist]]. He was the director of the [[McGill University]] AIDS Centre at the [[Montreal Jewish General Hospital]] and Professor of Medicine and of Microbiology at McGill University. His laboratory primarily studies HIV reverse transcriptase, the molecular basis for drug resistance, and gene therapy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/microimm/people/professors/wainberg|title=Mark Wainberg|date=7 April 2011|publisher=[[McGill University]]|access-date=9 July 2014}}</ref> He received a B.Sc. from McGill University in 1966, a Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]] in 1972, and did his post-doctoral research at [[Hadassah Medical School]] of the [[Hebrew University]].

==Accomplishments and honors==
Wainberg and his collaborators were the first to identify the antiviral capabilities of [[Lamivudine|3TC]] in 1989 and test the drug in patients. 3TC is also called [[lamivudine]].

From 1998 to 2000, Wainberg was President of the [[International AIDS Society]]. He was Co-Chair of the [[XVI International AIDS Conference, 2006|XVI International AIDS Conference]] and a past president of the [[Canadian Association for HIV Research]]. Wainberg founded the ''[[Journal of the International AIDS Society]]'' in 2004, which he was still supporting as one of its three Editors-in-Chief. He was also an editor on publications including the ''[[Journal of Human Virology]]'', ''[[Retrovirology (journal)|Retrovirology]],'' ''[[Journal of Leukocyte Biology]]'', ''[[International Medical Press|International Antiviral News]]'', ''[[AIDS Patient Care and STDs]]'', ''[[Brazilian Journal of Infectious Diseases]]'' and ''[[AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses]]''.

In 2001, he was made an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]], Canada's highest civilian honour, for his "major contributions to the study and treatment of" HIV/AIDS.<ref>{{OCC|5184}}</ref> In 2005, he was made an Officer of the [[National Order of Quebec]], an order of merit bestowed by the government of the Province of Quebec.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca/membres/membre.asp?id=1385|title=National Order of Quebec citation}}</ref> In 2000, he was made a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]. In 2008, Wainberg was named a Chevalier de [[Légion d'honneur]], the highest honor given by the country of [[France]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/canadian-hiv-expert-named-to-france-s-highest-order-1.769949|title=Canadian HIV expert named to France's highest order | work=CBC News | date=August 21, 2008}}</ref> In 2014, he was awarded the John G. Fitzgerald - CACMID Outstanding Microbiologist Award, which recognized him as "an individual who is outstanding in all aspects [and]... place him in a similar category to that of the individual the award is named after, Dr. [[John G. FitzGerald]]."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ammi.ca/media/65112/2014_finalprogram_web2.pdf|title=Final Program|publisher=[[Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada]]|access-date=9 July 2014|page=12|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714122151/http://www.ammi.ca/media/65112/2014_finalprogram_web2.pdf|archive-date=14 July 2014}}</ref> In 2016, he was inducted into the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cdnmedhall.org/inductees/markwainberg|title=Honouring Excellence &#124; Preserving History &#124; Inspiring Generations|access-date=2020-05-11|archive-date=2017-10-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171028221255/http://www.cdnmedhall.org/inductees/markwainberg|url-status=dead}}</ref> for his contributions to HIV/AIDS research.

Wainberg was also a past president of Congregation [[Tifereth Beth David Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://tbdj.org/leadership/|title=Congregation Tifereth Beth David Jerusalem leadership|work=TBDJ website|date=November 27, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120709184854/http://tbdj.org/leadership/|archive-date=July 9, 2012}}</ref>

On September 30, 2024 [[McGill University]] and the [[Montreal Jewish General Hospital]] established the Mark Wainberg Centre for Viral Diseases at McGill University<ref>{{Cite web |title=Name of pioneering HIV/AIDS researcher now adorns Centre for Viral Diseases |url=https://jghnews.ciussswestcentral.ca/name-of-pioneering-hiv-aids-researcher-now-adorns-centre-for-viral-diseases/ |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=JGH News |language=en-US}}</ref> in memory of the pioneering medical researcher.

==AIDS advocacy==
Dr. Wainberg advocated giving AIDS-related relief to developing countries. He was critical of politicians who ignore the problem of AIDS, including former South African President [[Thabo Mbeki]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Swarns |first=Rachel L. |title=South Africa Faults Critics of Its President on AIDS Stance |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 11, 2000 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/07/11/world/south-africa-faults-critics-of-its-president-on-aids-stance.html}}</ref> Dr. Wainberg also opposed the pseudoscientific ideas of [[AIDS denialism]] that are responsible for an estimated 330,000 AIDS deaths in South Africa alone.<ref>[http://www.hsph.harvard.edu/news/press-releases/2008-releases/researchers-estimate-lives-lost-delay-arv-drug-use-hivaids-south-africa.html Researchers Estimate Lives Lost Due to Delay in Antiretroviral Drug Use for HIV/AIDS in South Africa]</ref>

In 2006, Dr. Wainberg was the Co-Chair of the [[XVI International AIDS Conference, 2006|XVI International AIDS Conference]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20060813/aids_template_060813/20060813?hub=CTVNewsAt11|title=AIDS conference opens in Toronto without Harper|work=[[CTV Television Network|CTV]]}}{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} August 14, 2006</ref> In 2004, he was videotaped by AIDS denialist [[Robin Scovill]], whose HIV-positive wife died in 2008 and whose daughter died of untested and untreated AIDS in 2005.<ref name="LATimesArticle">[https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/901859901.html?dids=901859901:901859901&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Sep+24%2C+2005&author=Charles+Ornstein+and+Daniel+Costello&pub=Los+Angeles+Times&edition=&startpage=A.1&desc=A+Mother%27s+Denial%2C+a+Daughter%27s+Death A Mother's Denial, a Daughter's Death] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091120081531/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/901859901.html?dids=901859901:901859901&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Sep+24%2C+2005&author=Charles+Ornstein+and+Daniel+Costello&pub=Los+Angeles+Times&edition=&startpage=A.1&desc=A+Mother%27s+Denial%2C+a+Daughter%27s+Death |date=2009-11-20 }}: Article from L.A. Times, September 24, 2005</ref> In this interview, Dr. Wainberg proposed that those who harm others by publicly questioning HIV as the cause of AIDS should be charged with endangerment of public health and jailed if convicted of crime.

==Death==
Mark Wainberg drowned while on a vacation in Florida.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/mark-wainberg-montreal-aids-research-dies-2017-1.4067843 CBC April 12, 2017]</ref> Some believe he had an asthma attack in the water, while others believe the [[Undertow (water waves)|undertow]] dragged him out. His funeral was held on Friday, April 14, 2017, in Congregation Tifereth Beth David Jerusalem, the Montreal synagogue where he had previously served as president.
